extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset of over 100,000 crowdworker-written questions on Wikipedia articles, where each answer is a text span from the corresponding passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar; Jian Zhang; Konstantin Lopyrev; Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: selecting English Wikipedia articles and paragraphs, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs on those paragraphs, and collecting additional answers for development and test questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In additional answer collection, some questions were marked unanswerable by at least one crowdworker.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data came from sampled articles and extracted paragraphs from English Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Articles were sampled uniformly at random from the top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles by internal PageRank; paragraphs were extracted, images/figures/tables removed, short paragraphs discarded, and articles split randomly into train/dev/test.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included extracting paragraphs from Wikipedia articles, removing images, figures, and tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers wrote up to five questions per paragraph and highlighted answer spans in the paragraph. For development and test sets, at least two additional crowdworkers selected the shortest answer span for each question, or submitted the question without an answer if no span answered it.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was estimated using inter-annotator agreement from multiple answers per question; disagreement mainly came from inclusion or exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental answer disagreement.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 for training questions; at least 3 for development and test questions
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers had to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, at least 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to encourage exploration of more expressive models and advance reading comprehension research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Questions exhibit lexical and syntactic variation, and some examples are ambiguous; human mismatch often reflects span boundary differences.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Answers are constrained to spans in the passage rather than free-form responses; some questions are ambiguous or may not have a unique answer; 2.6% of development and test questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional annotator.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development/validation, and test for machine reading comprehension and question answering research.

We partitioned the articles randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: From each of these articles, we extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: On each paragraph, crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of that paragraph. The questions had to be entered in a text field, and the answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph... we obtained at least 2 additional answers for each question in the development and test sets... each crowdworker was shown only the questions along with the paragraphs of an article, and asked to select the shortest span in the paragraph that answered the question. If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer.
